node_definition.done_when: Read section 13 of the-obligations-hook-reads-a-snapshot first. In reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py, payload_for and live_payload carry the snapshot's skipped-record findings, so the prompt and stop hooks name each skipped path; extend the live_payload parity check to them. In reckon/crew/review.py, stored_record returns the records it skipped to its caller rather than accumulating them in the module-level _SKIPPED_RECORDS, so a read outside a sweep never reaches a later sweep's findings. Also in obligation_snapshot.py, route _parse_instant (around line 184) through reckon._timestamps.parse_utc, keeping its policy that a timestamp with no zone is UTC; this is a peer's request carried here because this node holds the file. tests/test_skipped_record_reaches_the_checklist.py, in a temporary configuration home, asserts a skipped record appears in the rendered prompt-path line, and that a read outside a sweep leaves the next sweep's findings unchanged. tests/test_unreadable_review_record_is_reported.py, tests/test_obligations_hook_reads_the_snapshot.py and tests/test_stop_hook_reads_the_snapshot.py keep passing. Record the outcome in docs/evidence/fragments/the-obligations-hook-reads-a-snapshot/skipped-record-reaches-the-checklist.html. Run `date -u` first and treat that instant as your start; your deadline is 60 minutes later. Write your manifest before starting any long command. Run both gate arms with pytest-xdist (-n 8 --timeout=300), never serially. Run the base arm, from a `git archive` extraction of your base under /tmp in a directory named for this run, and then the head arm, each in the foreground: a background command dies when your turn ends. Keep the gate to the test files that reach your change, tens of files rather than hundreds. Each arm uses its own basetemp outside any repository and writes to its own new log path, which it never overwrites. Each arm is recorded as JSON carrying completed true and a literal command with absolute paths and no angle-bracket placeholder. Each log names its revision on the first line as revision= followed by the full sha, and ends with a bare line reading EXIT= followed by the exit code. The head arm adds no failure id; any added id means status blocked, naming each id. ruff check and ruff format --check over the changed Python paths report no finding the base did not. Scratch goes under /tmp in a directory named for this run and is deleted before status complete. The turn ends once the manifest reads complete or blocked.
